stem: When is a capital redemption reserve created?

options.content: When shares are redeemed out of distributable profits
options.rationale: Correct: it replaces the capital that is repaid.

options.content: When shares are issued at a premium to investors
options.rationale: A premium is credited to share premium.

options.content: When non-current assets are revalued upwards
options.rationale: That creates a revaluation reserve.

options.content: When an interim dividend is paid to shareholders
options.rationale: A dividend reduces retained earnings only.

explanation: The CRR is credited when shares are redeemed or bought back from distributable profits, to maintain the capital of the company.

stem: Out of which sources may a company lawfully redeem its shares?

options.content: Distributable profits or the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares
options.rationale: Correct: neither source reduces the protection of creditors.

options.content: The share premium account and the revaluation reserve together
options.rationale: These are capital reserves and are not used to repay shares.

options.content: The proceeds of new loan notes issued to the bank only
options.rationale: Loan notes are not a permitted source.

options.content: Any bank balance that the company holds at the time of redemption
options.rationale: Cash alone is not a source of lawful funds.

explanation: Redemption is allowed from distributable profits or from the proceeds of a fresh issue of shares made for that purpose.

stem: What is the capital redemption reserve?

options.content: A distributable reserve that may be paid out as a dividend each year
options.rationale: The CRR is not distributable.

options.content: A liability owed to the former preference shareholders after redemption
options.rationale: The shareholders have been paid; it is not a liability.

options.content: A non-distributable reserve that maintains the capital of the company
options.rationale: Correct: it cannot be paid out as a dividend.

options.content: An asset representing the cash that was set aside for the redemption
options.rationale: It is part of equity, not an asset.

explanation: The CRR is part of equity, is not distributable and may only be used for a bonus issue.

stem: A company redeems 60,000 preference shares of US\$1 at par wholly out of distributable profits, without a new issue. What is credited to the capital redemption reserve?

options.content: Nil
options.rationale: A transfer is needed because no fresh issue was made.
Correct: the nominal value redeemed.
The amount is not doubled.

options.content: The cash paid less the premium
options.rationale: This is the cash, not the CRR; here the two are equal, but the rule is the nominal value.

explanation: With no fresh issue the CRR equals the nominal value redeemed, US\$60,000.
hints: Nominal value redeemed less the proceeds of any fresh issue.

stem: A company redeems 94,000 preference shares of US\$1 at par and finances part of this by issuing 38,000 ordinary shares of US\$1 at par. What is credited to the capital redemption reserve?

options.rationale: This ignores the fresh issue.
This is the fresh issue only.
Correct: 94,000 less 38,000.
The two amounts are added in error.

hints: CRR = nominal value redeemed - nominal value of the new shares.

stem: For which purpose may a company use its capital redemption reserve?

options.content: To pay an interim dividend
options.rationale: The CRR is not distributable.

options.content: To repay the loan notes
options.rationale: The CRR is not cash and cannot repay debt.

options.content: To write off the cost of a fresh issue
options.rationale: Share premium may do that, not the CRR.

options.content: To issue fully paid bonus shares
options.rationale: Correct: this keeps the capital in the company.

explanation: The CRR is used for a bonus issue; it cannot be distributed or used to repay liabilities.

stem: A company pays US\$50,000 in cash to redeem preference shares wholly from profits and credits US\$50,000 to the CRR. What is the effect on total equity?

options.content: It is unchanged, because the CRR replaces the shares
options.rationale: Cash has left the company.

options.content: It rises by US\$50,000, because a reserve is created
options.rationale: The reserve replaces the shares and retained earnings fall.

options.content: It falls by US\$100,000, because of both entries
options.rationale: The transfer is within equity.

options.content: It falls by US\$50,000, the cash paid out
options.rationale: Correct: the transfer to the CRR does not change the total.

explanation: Redeeming the shares removes US\$50,000 of share capital and cash. The transfer from retained earnings to the CRR only moves value within equity.

stem: The capital redemption reserve can be used to pay a dividend to ordinary shareholders.
explanation: False. It is a non-distributable reserve; it can only be used for a bonus issue.

stem: If shares are redeemed entirely from the proceeds of a fresh issue of the same nominal value, no capital redemption reserve is needed.
explanation: True. The capital is replaced by the new shares, so there is nothing to transfer to the CRR.
hints: How much capital has left the company?

stem: Match each entry in a redemption to the account that is credited.

left.content: Cash paid to the holders of the redeemed shares
Transfer to protect capital when shares are redeemed from profits
Proceeds of a fresh issue of shares at par

explanation: Cash paid credits Bank; the transfer credits the CRR; a fresh issue credits share capital; cancelling the shares debits their capital and credits Bank.
hints: Redeemed share capital is debited when it is cancelled.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: The capital redemption reserve is created by a transfer from {{blank:a}}. It is a {{blank:b}} reserve and cannot be paid as a dividend.

explanation: Profits are transferred from retained earnings to the CRR; the CRR is not distributable.

stem: What are the initials commonly used for the reserve created when shares are redeemed out of profits?
explanation: It is the capital redemption reserve (CRR).

stem: A company redeems 85,000 6% redeemable preference shares of US\$1 each at par, paying from the bank, with no fresh issue. Calculate the amount transferred to the capital redemption reserve.
explanation: With no fresh issue, the CRR equals the nominal value redeemed, US\$85,000.
workedSolution: 1. With no fresh issue, the CRR equals the nominal value redeemed, US\$85,000.

stem: A company redeems 140,000 redeemable preference shares of US\$1 at par. To help pay, it issues 55,000 new ordinary shares of US\$1 at par. The remainder is paid from distributable profits. Calculate the amount transferred to the capital redemption reserve.
explanation: 140,000 - 55,000 = US\$85,000. Using the whole redemption ignores the fresh issue, and using only the fresh issue is the wrong way round.
workedSolution: 1. 140,000 - 55,000 = US\$85,000. Using the whole redemption ignores the fresh issue, and using only the fresh issue is the wrong way round.
hints: CRR = nominal value redeemed - nominal value of the new issue.

stem: A company's retained earnings were US\$112,000. It redeems 48,000 preference shares of US\$1 at par out of profits with no fresh issue. Calculate retained earnings after the transfer to the capital redemption reserve.
explanation: Transfer = US\$48,000, so retained earnings = 112,000 - 48,000 = US\$64,000.
workedSolution: 1. Transfer = US\$48,000, so retained earnings = 112,000 - 48,000 = US\$64,000.
hints: Retained earnings fall by the amount transferred.

stem: A company redeems 72,000 9% preference shares of US\$1 each. Calculate the annual preference dividend that it no longer has to pay.
Explain why a company must create a capital redemption reserve when it redeems shares out of profits.

points.description: The redemption repays share capital, which reduces the cushion that protects creditors
Transferring profits to a non-distributable reserve keeps the total capital protection the same

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Repaying the shares reduces the capital that protects creditors. The transfer from distributable profits to the non-distributable CRR keeps the protection at the same level.

explanation: One mark for the reduction in protection and one for the effect of the CRR.

stem: Give two reasons why a company might prefer to redeem preference shares partly from a fresh issue of ordinary shares instead of wholly from cash.

points.description: It keeps cash in the business for operating needs or investment
Less distributable profit has to be converted to the non-distributable CRR, so more can be paid as dividends
Ordinary shares carry no compulsory dividend, unlike the preference shares replaced
The cost is that ownership and earnings are shared with new shareholders

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The cash stays in the business and less profit is locked into the CRR, so more is available for dividends. The ordinary shares have no fixed dividend, but the existing owners share their profits with the new shareholders.

explanation: One mark for each point, up to four.
hints: Think about cash and about distributable reserves.

stem: A company with US\$150,000 in the bank and distributable reserves of US\$170,000 plans to redeem 100,000 preference shares of US\$1 from profits. Evaluate the effect on the company and advise the directors.

points.description: Cash falls to US\$50,000, which may leave too little for operations and for paying creditors
Distributable reserves fall to US\$70,000 because US\$100,000 is moved to the CRR, so future dividends are limited
The company saves the fixed preference dividend
The CRR keeps the capital protection for creditors
Judgement: redeem only if enough cash remains for working capital, or use a fresh issue for part of the redemption

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Cash falls to US\$50,000, which may leave too little for working capital, and distributable reserves fall to US\$70,000, which limits dividends. The company saves the preference dividend and creditors stay protected. The directors should redeem only if cash remains adequate, or finance part with a fresh issue.

explanation: One mark each for cash, reserves, the dividend saving, creditor protection and a judgement.
hints: Work out the new cash and reserves first.
